location_source.description: These are the 200 locations on the Pennsylvania Department of Health roster of medical marijuana dispensaries with product, dated September 16, 2026 and retrieved October 28, 2026. The roster lists no permit numbers or counties. County and map points come from the U.S. Census Bureau Geocoder where it matched the exact address (163 of 200). Confirm hours, products and patient requirements with the store and the Department of Health.

pathways.next_step: Search the 200 Department of Health roster locations by city, county or distance, then confirm details with the store.
pathways.limitations: Denominator: all 200 rows of the Department of Health roster dated September 16, 2026. The roster is not a live permit list and names no permit holder. Store brands are grouped by the name printed on the roster, not by ownership. 37 locations have no county or map point because the Census geocoder did not match their exact address.

pathways.next_step: Read the home-cultivation rule; hemp growers can apply for a Department of Agriculture permit.
pathways.limitations: Home cultivation of cannabis is not allowed in Pennsylvania, so no seed sellers are listed. The one route is the Department of Agriculture hemp permit for licensed hemp growing.

pathways.next_step: Check what Clean Slate seals automatically, get your record, then use a local legal-help route or the Board of Pardons.
pathways.limitations: Statewide routes: State Police record access, Board of Pardons application and expedited review. Local free help found for Philadelphia (CLS, PLSE), Bucks, Chester, Delaware and Montgomery (LASP), Monroe and Pike (NPLS) and Allegheny (Public Defender's Project Reset). Neighborhood Legal Services and MidPenn Legal Services were checked: their current intake pages describe civil help only, and MidPenn's only record-clearing material found was an undated brochure and past clinics. Central and most of western Pennsylvania have no listed record-clearing help yet. No automatic cannabis relief beyond Clean Slate is claimed.

pathways.next_step: Read each dated summary, then the official statute it cites.
pathways.limitations: Six state-law summaries checked October 28, 2026 against the General Assembly's statute text: medical use limits, adult-use status and small-amount possession, home cultivation, employment protection, driving and Clean Slate sealing. Not legal advice. Local ordinances, hemp-derived products, Department of Health regulations and court orders are not summarized.

pathways.next_step: Register, find an approved practitioner, then check caregiver, fee and assistance options.
pathways.limitations: Official registration, approved practitioner list, caregiver rules, fee relief and purchase assistance, plus one funding-limited veteran fee reimbursement program. The practitioner list was not reviewed for location, fees or telehealth, and no individual eligibility is assessed.

pathways.next_step: Choose a provider type, such as testing labs, operators, banking, insurance, security, legal or consulting, and contact the provider.
pathways.limitations: Selected providers with Pennsylvania-specific sources: all five laboratories (six locations) on the Department of Health approved list, 11 operator brands with Pennsylvania retail or cultivation pages, two banks, two law practices, one consultancy, one trade association, one insurance agency and one security firm. This is not a list of all grower/processor permit holders. No packaging, equipment or technology providers with Pennsylvania evidence yet. A listing is not an endorsement.

pathways.next_step: Contact a group about meetings, membership or advocacy.
pathways.limitations: Six groups: a trade association, a legalization coalition, a veteran network and three NORML chapters (Bucks County, Lehigh Valley, Montco). No Pennsylvania cannabis events are verified for the next three months: organizer pages checked October 28, 2026 list the next Pennsylvania Cannabis Convention only as summer 2027 with no date, and NECANN's Philadelphia show as April 2028.

cards.name: Feel State
cards.description:
Cannabis Operator; Dispensary / Retail
Multi-state medical/adult-use dispensary operator, discovered via Pass 2 B2B relationship mapping rather than category research — surfaced no vendor edge itself but was found while researching a Sapphire/VALERE-adjacent facility search and independently confirmed as a genuine directory gap. Two confirmed Ohio locations: Urbana (962 N Main Street) and Lewis Center (8020 Orange Centre Drive), both showing active medical and adult-use sales on first-party location pages. UNCONFIRMED LINEAGE NOTE, flagged rather than asserted: an older BLOC website listed a coming-soon Urbana dispensary at this exact address (962 N Main Street) with this exact phone number (937-910-7744). Same facility and same phone number establish strong operational continuity but do NOT by themselves establish a corporate transaction, rebrand, license transfer, or ownership relationship between BLOC and Feel State — that would need a targeted DCC licensing/lineage check before being written as fact. DCC ROSTER CONFIRMATION (2026-08-16): the licensed legal entity behind both Ohio locations is Healing Through Cannabis LLC — Urbana (962 N. Main Street, CCD000019-00, Active) and Lewis Center (8020 Orange Center Drive, CCD000271-00, Active) are both confirmed current dispensary licenses under this exact name. Neither "Feel State" nor "BLOC" appears anywhere in the DCC roster as a licensed entity name — both are trade names/brands operating under Healing Through Cannabis LLC, not the legal entity itself. This confirms Feel State is a genuine, currently active Ohio operator at both addresses already on file. The BLOC lineage question is now narrower and more answerable: whether Healing Through Cannabis LLC previously operated as, or acquired, whatever entity used the BLOC brand at the same Urbana address/phone number — that is a rebrand/history question, not an active-license question, since the current license is unambiguous.

cards.name: Klutch Cannabis
cards.description:
Cannabis Operator
Confirmed via Ohio Cannabis Coalition coverage: Akron-based Klutch (founder Adam Thomarios) is an active Ohio cannabis operator/brand. Documented current brand-partnership relationships, independently corroborated from two separate sources: Klutch's own June 2026 Columbus-opening press release names Cookies, Josh D and Kiva Confections directly as brand partners carried alongside Klutch's house brands (Klutch Cannabis, Citizen by Klutch, Habitat by Klutch); Klutch's Featured Brands page separately confirms the same three and additionally states Josh D has been Klutch's Ohio partner since 2018 ("OG Ohio partner"). Also documented: an M&A/license-transfer relationship with Farkas Farms (also in this Directory) — DCC approved Klutch's June 2026 acquisition of Farkas Farms' Columbus dispensary license (5429 Bethel Sawmill Center), while Klutch simultaneously sold its Loudonville dispensary/license to Farkas Farms. Confirmed via eight independent sources including Crain's Cleveland Business. Vendor relationships, all current and confirmed via Klutch's own site: CannaPlanners (website/digital development — credited as site provider), Headset (brand-locator/data technology powering the statewide "Find Klutch Near Me" tool — narrow integration, not a broader analytics contract), Dutchie (Dutchie Pay accepted in-store), and CanPay (accepted cashless payment option). CannaPlanners, Headset, Dutchie and CanPay are all also entries in this Directory. Wholesale/distribution relationships into named current Ohio dispensary partners, per Klutch's own statewide locator: Ascend Cannabis, Amplify and Backroad Wellness (all three also entries in this Directory) are explicitly listed as current dispensary partners carrying Klutch products. Exact IRS classification remains unverified; current leadership claims should be independently corroborated before import. ENTITY LEGITIMACY FLAG — escalated, not merely unresolved. Independently checked directly: the site's own "About" page lists six leadership bios by first name only (John, Emma, Michael, Sarah, David, Karen) — no surnames, no verifiable specifics, no independently findable individuals anywhere else online. The bios read as generic template copy ("John brings strategic vision," "Emma has been growing hemp since the program's inception") rather than real staff descriptions. This pass separately found the domain itself listed for sale at $50,000+. Combined, this is stronger evidence than a normal "stale/under-researched" flag: it raises a real question of whether this is a genuine operating nonprofit at all, versus a placeholder or SEO/lead-gen site built to look like one. Recommend a decision — keep flagged as unverified, or move out of scope like One Bond Laboratories — rather than treating this as an ordinary open contact-research row. FINAL DISPOSITION: moved out of scope rather than left open indefinitely. This is now the second independent research pass to flag the same problem — a domain-for-sale Contact page (asking $50,000+) alongside leadership bios ("John," "Emma," "Michael," "Sarah," "David," "Karen" — first names only, generic template copy) that no independent source, including Ohio-government or credible organizational records, corroborates. Two separate research passes plus this Directory's own direct check of the site all converge on the same conclusion: there is no verifiable evidence this represents a genuine operating nonprofit, as distinct from a placeholder or SEO/lead-gen site built to resemble one. Handled the same way as One Bond Laboratories — retained as a record with full provenance rather than deleted, excluded from the publishable count, so a future pass does not re-research or re-add it without new evidence.

rules.summary: Medical use is lawful only under the Medical Marijuana Act: a registered patient or caregiver with a Department of Health ID card and practitioner certification. A dispensary may not dispense more than a 90-day supply. Smoking medical marijuana is unlawful; patients and caregivers may make edibles themselves.

sources.limitations: General Assembly compilation of the Medical Marijuana Act, showing amendments through Act 63 of 2023 and a compiler's note on Act 45 of 2025. Regulations, Department of Health notices and court orders also apply and are not summarized here. Not legal advice.

rules.summary: Pennsylvania has no adult-use (recreational) cannabis law. Without a medical card, possessing up to 30 grams of marijuana or 8 grams of hashish for personal use is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 30 days in jail, a fine of up to $500, or both. Some cities have their own ordinances; this summary covers state law only.

sources.limitations: General Assembly compilation of the Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act. Local ordinances, charging practices and diversion programs are not covered. Not legal advice.
Advocacy organization's October 13, 2026 post. Used only for the current absence of an adult-use law; its election commentary is not used.

rules.summary: Home cultivation is not allowed. Only grower/processors permitted by the Department of Health may grow medical marijuana, and Pennsylvania has no adult-use home-grow law. Growing hemp requires a separate Department of Agriculture permit.

sources.limitations: General Assembly compilation of the Medical Marijuana Act, showing amendments through Act 63 of 2023 and a compiler's note on Act 45 of 2025. Regulations, Department of Health notices and court orders also apply and are not summarized here. Not legal advice.

rules.summary: An employer may not fire, refuse to hire or otherwise discriminate against someone solely because they are certified to use medical marijuana. Employers need not allow use at work and may discipline employees for being under the influence at work when their conduct falls below the standard of care for the job.

sources.limitations: General Assembly compilation of the Medical Marijuana Act, showing amendments through Act 63 of 2023 and a compiler's note on Act 45 of 2025. Regulations, Department of Health notices and court orders also apply and are not summarized here. Not legal advice.

rules.summary: Driving with any amount of a Schedule I controlled substance or its metabolite in your blood is DUI, whether or not you are impaired. Marijuana is a Schedule I substance under Pennsylvania law, and the DUI statute has no exception for medical marijuana patients.

sources.limitations: The effective date shown is the earliest date in the General Assembly's source note; the subsection may be older. Statute text of 75 Pa.C.S. § 3802. Court decisions, testing practice and penalties under other sections are not summarized. Not legal advice.

rules.summary: Clean Slate limits access to (seals) certain records automatically: charges that did not end in a conviction; summary convictions after five years; and second- and third-degree misdemeanors and misdemeanors punishable by up to two years after seven years free of convictions punishable by a year or more. Court-ordered restitution must be paid. A pardon is a separate step.

sources.limitations: Exclusions in the statute apply. Statute text of 18 Pa.C.S. § 9122.2. Whether a particular record qualifies depends on the full record, restitution and exclusions in the statute. Not legal advice.
